lesson.title: Calendar Gym
lesson.subtitle: Monday to Saturday, and the days that take op

hook.title: Seven Days, One Frame
hook.content: Maandag through zaterdag: each day is a name you can read, and each one takes op when you say what happens on it. The frame never changes; the day does.

pattern.title: Op + day
pattern.content: Op maandag werk ik, op dinsdag kom ik, op zaterdag ben ik vrij. The preposition op marks the day; the verb keeps V2 order.
pattern.trap_note: The day name looks like an adverb, but it still needs op when it is a time phrase: op maandag, not maandag werk ik in formal writing (though the bare form occurs in speech).

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Calendar Gym):
exercises.target_answer: de maandag, de dinsdag, de woensdag, de donderdag, de vrijdag, de zaterdag
exercises.meaning: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Calendar Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Vandaag is het maandag.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Calendar Gym”.
“Morgen is het dinsdag.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Op + day.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: The day name looks like an adverb, but it still needs op when it is a time phrase: op maandag, not maandag werk ik in formal writing (though the bare form occurs in speech).

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Woensdag werk ik.” is word-for-word “Wednesday work I.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Op + day.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: On Saturday it is free.
exercises.explanation: “Zaterdag is het vrij.” reuses only material taught in “Calendar Gym” — Op + day.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Zaterdag is het vrij.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Op + day.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “On Sunday it is quiet.”
twist.explanation: Zondag is the last day of the set; rustig describes the day.

summary.outcome: Say what happens on each day with the op-frame or a fronted day.
summary.takeaway: Day names are vocabulary; the time phrase is the grammar.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: The Weak Past.

maandag.etymology_derivation: A day named for the moon, like English Monday.

dinsdag.etymology_derivation: A day named for an old Germanic god, like English Tuesday.

woensdag.etymology_derivation: Named for Woden, like English Wednesday.

donderdag.etymology_derivation: Named for Thor, like English Thursday.

vrijdag.etymology_derivation: Named for Frigg, like English Friday.

zaterdag.etymology_derivation: Named for Saturn, like English Saturday.
